findings.body: The check matches only the English text `Default Version: 2`. WSL localizes that label—for example, its [Japanese status resource](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/blob/master/localization/strings/ja-JP/Resources.resw) uses a different label. On a Windows laptop with WSL2 already ready, `-Check` therefore reports it missing, and a full run repeatedly enters the WSL installation path. Determine readiness without matching an English label.
findings.title: Recognize localized WSL2 status

findings.body: Any directory with each browser prefix counts as installed, including an incomplete download or revisions left by an older Playwright release. Windows makes the same check at `scripts/install-windows.ps1:21`. Check mode can report nothing missing even though Playwright cannot launch a browser: [Playwright requires binaries matched to its version](https://playwright.dev/docs/browsers). Check the required browser revisions before skipping installation.
findings.title: Check usable Playwright browsers before skipping installation

findings.body: A standalone `docker` CLI makes this script skip Docker Desktop; Windows uses the same command-only check at `scripts/install-windows.ps1:72`. After a fresh Desktop installation, neither script tells the user to launch it, so setup can finish without a usable Docker engine. Check Desktop separately and print the first-launch action. Docker's [Mac](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/mac-install/) and [Windows](https://docs.docker.com/desktop/setup/install/windows-install/) instructions both require starting Desktop.
findings.title: Check Docker Desktop and tell the user to start it
